gen-fs-nippo-gf-radio-canada: Crisp and technical, Nippo lifts its small letters almost to capital height, and Radio Canada backs it with full, tall lowercase. Shrink Nippo and that wire-cut bite gets lost.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-radio-canada-big: Contemporary through and through, Nippo leads with small letters standing proud. Radio Canada Big takes over below with open-ended strokes and a monoline build, giving the heading's wire-cut edge a plain sans to rest on.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads steadily, with broad gaps at the terminals and an unvarying weight from word to word. Nippo adds a technical edge up top, with proud small letters and wire-cut strokes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-ruda: Approachable and clean, Ruda has wide-mouthed rounds and a sizable x-height in its lowercase. Nippo and Ruda both look drawn with wire, and that shared thread is what holds the pair.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-saira: Clean lines run through Nippo, its small letters standing proud and drawn with one constant pen width. Saira, a sans-serif with see-through s shapes and tall rounds, gives Nippo's constant line a rounder partner.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch is approachable and easygoing, its lowercase e opening clearly and its ascenders sitting close above the x-height. Nippo above it has no calligraphic shading to guide the eye.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Nippo stands its small letters nearly capital-tall and drops hairlines from the alphabet entirely, so every stroke looks cut from wire. Schibsted Grotesk adds big, open e and a shapes beneath it.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-ubuntu-sans: Small letters rising nearly to capital height give Nippo its wire-cut, technical look, while Ubuntu Sans bends in tubular strokes. Wire meets copper pipe, and that shared metalwork feel is the draw.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-epilogue: Panchang draws steady strokes with open space around every stem and curve. Epilogue follows with curvy, unclamped lowercase and stubby ascender tips, which keeps running text feeling friendly, line after line.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-supreme: A ruler-drawn, constant-width line runs straight through Panchang, with generous stretches of open space between each stem and curve. Panchang grabs attention; Supreme holds a thick, crisp band of text.
